THE COMPLETE DOCTOR ACADEMYMRCPsych Paper A · Domain 2 Neuroscience · 2027 syllabus

Aim and objectives

Aim. To prepare you to explain the integrated neurobiology of sleep, genetic, eating, epileptic, personality, multimorbid and menstrual disorders for MRCPsych Paper A.

At the end of this chapter, you should be able to:

  1. Explain narcolepsy as loss of orexin neurones and delayed sleep phase as a disorder of circadian timing.
  2. Match genetic syndromes to mechanisms: FMR1 expansion in fragile X, 15q11-13 imprinting in Prader-Willi and Angelman, and 22q11.2 deletion.
  3. Describe the neurobiology of anorexia nervosa, including starvation effects and altered reward and anxiety circuits.
  4. Explain how temporal lobe seizures cause pre-ictal, ictal, postictal and interictal psychiatric symptoms, including postictal psychosis.
  5. Describe amygdala hyperreactivity with weak prefrontal control in personality disorder, and shared stress and inflammatory biology in multimorbidity.
  6. Explain premenstrual dysphoric disorder as abnormal brain sensitivity to normal hormone changes, including the neurosteroid allopregnanolone.
  7. Answer the chapter's 90 exam-style questions, scoring at least 80%, by the end of this chapter.
